page.title: Calibrate
page.subtitle: Configure module routing, the camera scan region, and servo calibration

moduleCountStepper.label: Sorting modules
moduleCountStepper.description: How many physical sorting modules are wired up. Changes the number of bins available and the sections below.

reduceConfirm.title: Reduce module count?
reduceConfirm.description: Dropping to {{count}} modules will permanently delete the sorting rules and calibration data for modules and bins beyond that count, across every bin preset. This can't be undone.

channelLayoutUpgrade.banner: This sorter uses the deprecated legacy channel layout, capped at 3 modules. Rewire module 1 to start at channel 0, then update to the standard layout to support up to 5 modules.
channelLayoutUpgrade.confirmDescription: Only do this after rewiring module 1 to start at PCA9685 channel 0 (module 2 at 3, module 3 at 6, feeder right after the last module). Until then, the servos will move on the wrong channels. The legacy layout can't be selected again afterwards.
channelLayoutUpgrade.done: Switched to the standard channel layout.
channelLayoutUpgrade.failed: Couldn't switch the channel layout. Try again.

experimentalFeatures.title: Experimental
experimentalFeatures.pipelinedFeedLabel: Scan the next card while sorting
experimentalFeatures.pipelinedFeedDescription: Feeds and scans the next card as soon as the previous one has left module 1, instead of waiting for it to reach its bin. Needs firmware 2.1.0 or newer and auto-feed turned on. Turn this off if cards jam or scans start picking up the moving card.

feederCalibrationPanel.heading: Feeder
feederCalibrationPanel.speedTooltip: How fast and which way the feeder motor spins. 0% is stopped; drag either way to speed up in that direction.
feederCalibrationPanel.settleDurationDescription: Extra time to keep feeding once the module 1 sensor sees the last card in the hopper, so it travels all the way into the mechanism before the motor stops.
feederCalibrationPanel.reverseDurationDescription: Once a card reaches module 1, spin the roller backward this long so the next card in the hopper is pulled back instead of creeping forward into a double feed. 0 turns it off.

irSensorPanel.label: IR Sensors
irSensorPanel.tooltip: Infrared sensors that detect when a card is present at each module's feed path
irSensorPanel.monitorTooltip: Continuously poll the IR sensors and update the badges below in real time
irSensorPanel.readTooltip: Take a single snapshot reading of the IR sensors
irSensorPanel.detectedTooltip: A card is currently detected at Module {{module}}'s IR sensor
irSensorPanel.notDetectedTooltip: No card currently detected at Module {{module}}'s IR sensor
irSensorPanel.hopperTooltip: Whether the card hopper's IR sensor currently detects cards waiting to be fed

moduleCalibrationGrid.noPositionSelected: Select a position above to edit it
moduleCalibrationGrid.percentSliderTooltip: How far this servo is pushed, as a percent of its full range of motion. Select a position above, then drag this slider to change it - it's saved along with everything else when you hit Save.
moduleCalibrationGrid.rawPulseTooltip: Raw servo pulse position (120-490), the exact value sent to the device.
moduleCalibrationGrid.testServoTooltipGate: Test: briefly opens the gate, then returns it to closed, so you can watch it move.
moduleCalibrationGrid.testServoTooltipPusher: Test: briefly fires the pusher left, then right, then returns it to neutral, so you can watch it move both ways.
moduleCalibrationGrid.pusherOffsetWarning: More than {{percent}}% away from neutral. The arm shouldn't touch the inner wall, and the further out you push it, the higher the risk of skipping gears or the horn shifting on the shaft.
moduleCalibrationGrid.pusherHoldDurationDescription: How long the pusher stays extended before returning to neutral. Longer if cards aren't pushed fully out before it retracts; keep it short, since holding against the end stop strains the servo horn.
moduleCalibrationGrid.paddleCloseDelayDescription: How long after the pusher fires before this module's paddle closes again, independent of the pusher's own return timing. Longer if cards aren't fully clear before the gate shuts.
moduleCalibrationGrid.pushTestTooltip: Runs this module's push exactly as a route would, using the hold time and paddle close delay above (even before you save them). No card is fed; drop one onto the module first to see it pushed out.

scanRegionCalibrationPanel.instructions: Drag the box to move it, or drag the handle to resize. Line it up with a card sitting at module 1.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.liveDetectionHint: The dashed box is the fallback crop used when live detection can't find the card - it's what you're editing. The solid outline is a live preview of what detection sees.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.captureSettleDescription: How long to wait after the feeder confirms a card has arrived before capturing a frame, so the card is fully still and in focus.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.matchesNeededDescription: How many consecutive frames must agree on the same card before a scan is accepted. 1 is fastest; higher values are more reliable but slower.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.checkBothOrientationsDescription: Also match the card rotated 180°, so cards fed upside down are still identified. Turn off if all your cards are fed the same way up to make each scan faster.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.executionProviderDescription: Which backend runs the card-detection and matching models in your browser. WASM is the default and works everywhere. WebGPU can be faster on some GPUs, and falls back to WASM if it fails to start.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.takePhotoPrompt: Take a photo from your phone to position the box.
scanRegionCalibrationPanel.phoneCaptureFailed: Phone didn't respond with a photo in time.

toasts.notCalibratedDescription: Configure all three modules before running the test sequence.
toasts.importInvalid: That file isn't a valid calibration export
toasts.saveCalibrationFailed: Failed to save the scan region or capture settle delay
toasts.pushTestUnsupported: This firmware doesn't support push tests. Update the sorter firmware.

dialog.title: Calibration differs from the sorter
dialog.description: {{name}} has calibration saved on it that doesn't match the calibration saved in the app. Choose which one to keep.
dialog.hint: Using the app's calibration overwrites the sorter's. Using the sorter's saves its values to the app, where you can still undo them from the calibration history.

toasts.adopted: Saved the sorter's calibration to the app
toasts.adoptFailed: Couldn't save the sorter's calibration, using the app's instead
toasts.storeFailed: Couldn't save calibration on the sorter

setupWizard.forced: Setup wizard required for this sorter

setupWizard.title: Set up your sorter

intro.heading: Let's calibrate this sorter
intro.body: Every servo stops in a slightly different place, so each position needs setting once before this sorter can run. This walks through them one at a time. Every slider moves the real servo as you drag it, so watch the sorter while you adjust.

feeder.name: Feeder
feeder.desc: The roller under the hopper that pulls one card at a time into module 1.

module.name: Modules
module.desc: The stacked sorting stages. Each one catches the card, then pushes it into one of its two bins or drops it to the module below.

bottom.name: Bottom paddle
bottom.desc: The trapdoor floor of each module. Closed holds the card, open drops it to the next module.

paddle.name: Paddles
paddle.desc: The side gates. They hold the card in place and open to let it be pushed out.

pusher.name: Pusher
pusher.desc: The arm that sweeps the card sideways into a bin.

intro.skipNote: You can skip this and calibrate later from the Calibration page.

moduleCount.heading: How many modules does this sorter have?
moduleCount.body: Count the sorting modules stacked on this sorter, not including the feeder. Each module adds two bins.

servos.bottom: The bottom paddle is the module's trapdoor floor. It holds the card while the module decides where it goes.
servos.paddle: The paddles are the side gates. They keep the card in place until it's pushed out to a bin.
servos.pusher: The pusher is the arm that sweeps the card sideways out of the module into one of its two bins.

bottomClosed.title: Bottom paddle: closed
bottomClosed.body: Drag until the trapdoor sits flat and fully shut, so a card resting on it can't slip through. Stop as soon as it's closed; pushing further strains the servo.

bottomOpen.title: Bottom paddle: open
bottomOpen.body: Drag until the trapdoor swings fully open and a card would drop cleanly to the module below. Stop where it stops moving.

paddleClosed.title: Paddles: closed
paddleClosed.body: Drag until the paddles close in and hold a card in place without pinching it.

paddleOpen.title: Paddles: open
paddleOpen.body: Drag until the paddles open wide enough for a card to slide out sideways.

pusherNeutral.title: Pusher: neutral
pusherNeutral.body: Drag until the arm sits centered and clear of the card path, so cards drop straight past it.

pusherLeft.title: Pusher: left
pusherLeft.body: Drag until the arm swings toward the inner wall of the module, pushing a card out on the right side as you face the sorter. Stop before the arm touches the wall, about {{min}}-{{max}}% away from neutral. The pusher doesn't need to hit the wall to fling the card, and pressing against it strains the servo.

pusherRight.title: Pusher: right
pusherRight.body: Now the other way: drag until the arm swings toward the inner wall on the other side, pushing a card out on the left side as you face the sorter. Again, stop before it touches the wall, about {{min}}-{{max}}% away from neutral.

irSensors.heading: Check the sensors
irSensors.body: Each module has an infrared sensor at its gate that sees when a card arrives, and one more in the hopper that sees when cards are waiting. Hold a card in front of each sensor, one at a time, and watch its row light up. Each sensor gets a check once it has seen a card.
irSensors.moduleHint: Hold a card where the card rests in this module.
irSensors.hopperHint: Put a few cards in the hopper.
irSensors.waiting: Waiting for the first reading from the sorter…
irSensors.footnote: A sensor that never lights up is usually unplugged, wired to the wrong pin, or pointed away from the card path. You can continue and fix it later.

feeder.heading: Feeder speed
feeder.body: The feeder roller pulls the bottom card out of the hopper and into module 1. Drag until it spins in the direction that pulls cards in, at a steady speed.
feeder.hint: 0% is stopped. Drag either way to spin it in that direction. It stops on its own a few seconds after you let go.

test.heading: Run the self-test
test.body: The sorter opens every trapdoor and paddle, sweeps every pusher both ways, then briefly spins the feeder. Make sure no cards are in the modules, then run it.
test.passed: Test passed. This sorter is ready to use.
test.failedHint: Go back and adjust any position that didn't move cleanly, then run the test again.

connectionSettings.title: Connection
connectionSettings.autoConnectDescription: When this sorter is plugged in over USB while the app is open (or is already plugged in when the app loads), it connects on its own and runs its self-test so it's ready to scan. Over Bluetooth, if it drops or is power-cycled, the app keeps trying to reconnect until the tab is closed. Connect it by hand once in this browser first, so the browser allows it.
connectionSettings.testOnConnectDescription: When on, the sorter cycles every servo and checks its sensors each time it connects. When off, it only loads its saved calibration and is ready right away. You can still run the test from the calibration page.

firmware.title: Firmware
firmware.description: Check which firmware the sorter is running and update it from this browser.
firmware.bluetoothNote: Flashing doesn't work over Bluetooth. Connect the sorter with a USB cable to flash it.
firmware.unoNote: Arduino Uno R4 boards can't be flashed from the browser. Download the firmware and upload it with the Arduino IDE.
firmware.notConnectedHint: Connect a sorter to see its version, or flash an ESP32-S3 over USB without connecting it first.
firmware.unsupported: This browser can't flash boards. Use Chrome or Edge on a computer.
